fields.Q1:
WHAT IS STANDING AROUND THIS ROOM MADE OF?**
Grey stone block, laid in courses, cracked. But I want to be honest about how I know that: **at 1:1 I could not tell.** At the size shown, every standing surface in this frame is a near-black field. I named the material only after brightening the file 7×.
fields.Q1_WHY: Measured mean luminance of each wall band — north (y150–225, x60–690) **10.1**; west (x5–50, y300–560) **8.9**; east (x700–748) **7.2**; south (y790–826) **10.7**. p5→p95 spread inside those bands is roughly 2→15. That is a thirteen-level range, about 5% of the display range. The floor beside the figure runs mean 117, p95 167. Saturation max across the west, east and south bands is **4** — the walls are colourless. Under 7× gain the courses resolve: irregular rectangular blocks with dark grout on the north and west, and on the south **no courses at all** — just a smooth vertical gradient.
fields.Q2:
SOLID MASS, OR FLAT PATTERN AROUND THE EDGE?**
**Flat pattern**, with one exception.

Row y=470 (the figure's own row), crossing the west edge: x=40–54 reads **[11,11,14]**; x=55 drops to **[3,3,3]**; x=56–80 (floor) reads **3 to 8**. The wall is *brighter than the floor it stands on*. No side face, no cast shadow, no occlusion, no thickness ramp — the wall has no lighting relationship to the torch at all. It sits at a flat ambient ~10 whether it is 200px from the flame or 600px: north band near the light 10.2, north band far right (x560–690) 9.9. Identical.

The exception: a ~26px strip at y=234–260 along the north edge only, subdivided by short vertical ticks, which reaches mean 18.9 / max 35 above the figure. That one strip reads as a face. Nothing equivalent exists on the west, east or south sides.
fields.Q3:
WHERE EXACTLY DOES THE GROUND STOP?**
Two places, both **two pixels wide**.

North, at x=300: y=228 is **21**, y=230–232 is **4** (a black grout line), y=234 is **13**. Two pixels. Then the base strip climbs 13→17 across y=234–260, a second 2px black line at y=262–264, and the floor proper from y=266 at **18**, rising to 60 by y=290.

West, at y=470: **x=54 is 11, x=55 is 3.** One pixel. That is the entire transition.

Nothing else happens across either boundary. No bevel, no contact shadow, no dust or rubble line, no highlight on the near lip. A grout line, and the value goes the wrong way.
fields.Q4:
WHAT IS HOLDING THIS PLACE TOGETHER?**
**NOTHING.**

Not a hedge — a measurement. Maximum saturation across the west, east and south wall bands is **4 out of 255**, and 0–1% of pixels in those bands are warm (R>B). There is no rope, no driven pin, no timber, no hide, no iron, no bracket, no rust, no shim, no patch anywhere on any standing surface in this frame. Four hundred years of a repair company, and there is not one fastener on the wall.
fields.Q5:
BUILT, OR REPEATED?**
**Repeated.** I have pixel-exact proof.

I extracted every connected black decal on the wall bands and compared them. Five pairs are **byte-identical, pixel for pixel**:

| shape | instance A | instance B | offset |
|---|---|---|---|
| 30×14 solid bar | (15,170) | (207,170) | +192px = 3 tiles |
| 14×56 crack | (41,140) | (233,140) | +192px = 3 tiles |
| 38×60 crack | (251,8) | (315,8) | **+64px = 1 tile** |
| 38×62 crack | (251,70) | (315,134) | **+64,+64 = 1 tile diagonally** |
| 33×62 crack | (0,262) | (0,710) | +448px = 7 tiles |

The same crack sprite appears in two horizontally adjacent tiles (row 3), and again in two diagonally adjacent tiles (row 4). The underlying block texture does vary — the full 192px block is only ~30% identical — so it is the damage layer specifically that is stamped from a tiny set. The cracks are the only thing that reads as history, and the cracks are a repeating stamp.

Corroboration on the south wall: I found the black zigzags at x-centres 19, 84, 155, 211, 283, 347, 426, 516, 580, 659, 746. Deltas 65, 71, 56, 72, 64, 79, 64, 79, 87 — one crack per 64px tile, each roughly mid-tile.
fields.Q6:
WOULD YOU BELIEVE THIS SHIPPED?**
**YES** — plenty of shipped games render walls as a dark band.

Merely competent, or genuinely good? **Merely competent, and only in the file.** On screen it is below competent, because the competent part is invisible. The top-lit block work, the base strip, the ladder-shaped glyph at (132,188)–(150,225) — that is real craft, and none of it is on the player's screen.
fields.Q7:
WHAT CAN YOU ACTUALLY SEE ON THE STANDING SURFACES AT 1:1?**

Legible at 1:1:
- North band (y150–228): a near-black field with a handful of black squiggles, and the horizontal edge line at y≈230.
- West band (x0–55): flat near-black; one or two black marks around y=390–480.
- **East band (x690–750): blank. Nothing.**
- **South band (y782–828): blank. Nothing.**

Only after magnifying: the course/block grid on all sides; the base strip's vertical tick divisions; the solid black bars at (15,170) and (207,170); the ladder/spine glyph at (132,188); the pale ellipse blobs on the base strip at (75–85, 243) and (131–147, 236); every crack's actual shape.

Does it change with distance from the figure? **Almost not at all, and that is the problem.** North near-light 10.2 vs north far-right 9.9 — a 0.3-level difference across 500px. The single exception is the north base strip directly above the figure (y232–260, x330–470) at mean 18.9, max 35. That is the brightest wall pixel in the entire frame: **35/255, or 14% grey.** The wall never catches the light. The light pool stops dead at the floor line.
fields.Q8:
ANYTHING YOUR EYE KEEPS RETURNING TO?**
Yes, three things.

1. **The vertical zigzag.** The same black squiggle motif appears on all four bands at roughly one per 64px tile, near tile centre. On the south band it is the *only* content — a smooth grey gradient with an evenly-spaced picket fence of identical squiggles. Once seen it cannot be unseen.
2. **The solid black horizontal bars, all at y=170.** (15,170) and (207,170) are the same 30×14 rectangle, and they sit on the same scanline 192px apart.
3. **The two black rectangles at the top**, (0,6)–(246,133) and (567,6)–(749,133), RGB **(1,1,2)** — axis-aligned, hard-edged, absolute black.
fields.Q9:
WHAT IS BEYOND THE WALLS?**
Two different answers, and neither is a place.

Along the top, beyond the north wall: **absolute void** — those two rectangles at RGB (1,1,2), with mathematically hard rectangular edges. Not darkness that falls off; a value floor with a corner in it. It reads as a UI mask, not as space.

On the west, east and south: **there is no beyond.** The wall band simply runs to the edge of the frame at a flat ~9 and is cut off by the screen. The wall has no far side, no thickness, no next thing. Asked to say which of your four options it is — it is none of them. It is not more of the same stuff, not empty space, not an unseen room. It is the edge of the drawing.
fields.Q10:
COULD YOU TELL A WAY THROUGH WITHOUT WALKING INTO IT?**
I found it — **and I read it as a notch, not a passage.**

The corridor is x≈382–433, running north from y=228. Measured: at y=150–225, the flanking wall averages 13.8 and the corridor floor averages **11.1**. The passage is *darker than the wall beside it*, by 2.7 levels — about 1% of the display range, and the wrong sign. At the corridor mouth (y=200–228) the difference is **0.9 levels**. That is noise.

What I actually saw at 1:1 were two thin dark vertical seams at x≈375–382 and x≈433–438, and I wrote them down as a seam in the pattern. I only resolved it as a corridor two ways: by brightening 7×, and by reading the minimap at (700,5)–(750,55), which plainly shows a lower room, a one-tile vertical corridor, and an upper room.

So: the answer to your question is **no**. The minimap tells you there is a way through. The dungeon does not.
fields.Q11:
HAS ANYTHING HAPPENED TO THIS STRUCTURE?**
It is cracked, uniformly, everywhere, by the same crack. Nothing else has happened to it.

I read that from: identical crack sprites one tile apart (Q5); constant crack pitch (~64px) on the south band; no rubble at any wall base; no differential wear — the wall in the trafficked corridor mouth is textured the same as the wall in the dead south corner; no repair of any kind (Q4); and no breach, spall, bulge, lean or settle anywhere along 2,700px of wall run. This is not a structure that has been in heavy use since before records began. It is a structure that had a damage decal applied to it evenly, once.
fields.CULL: No wall pixel in this frame exceeds 35/255. The material is invisible at play size.
fields.FLIP LIST:
- Let the torch light the walls. The nearest wall face must reach the value the floor reaches at the same distance — the north strip should be reading 60–90, not 19. Right now the light pool stops at the floor line.
- Give the wall thickness the player can see: a lit near-face along the north edge and a cast contact shadow onto the floor at the west, east and south edges. Currently the west wall at (54,470) is *brighter* than the floor at (56,470).
- Kill the duplicate decals. (251,8)/(315,8) and (251,70)/(315,134) are the same crack in adjacent and diagonally-adjacent tiles; (15,170)/(207,170) is the same bar on the same scanline. Vary or mirror per instance, and break the one-crack-per-tile rhythm on the south band.
- Put the orc repair on the wall — rope, driven pins, salvaged timber, hide. Max saturation on three of four wall bands is currently 4; there is nothing warm, nothing structural, nothing fastened anywhere.
- Make the north corridor mouth readable without the minimap. It is currently 0.9 luminance levels different from the wall beside it, and darker. It needs a visible jamb.

Model: Claude Opus 5 (1M context).
